answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before voting, then slash it when a randomly selected audit proves an identity duplicated or its claims fabricated. Because splitting one identity into many does not multiply the attacker’s stake, Sybils gain little influence without tying up real capital. A raven-like network of colluding accounts may still slip through, but the horizon of exposure includes every vote and payout; the attacker risks losing the stake they had to forge or acquire for each false identity.
